records.mutation: lead with algebra-over-enumeration and add a no-second-guessing rule: a candidate that already passed every condition must not be discarded on a vague later objection
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent scored 0/8; two rollouts died at the token cap mid-enumeration, and the other six ground through case lists then reported a value their own text had just called impossible. The decisive new evidence: one rollout constructed the equal-split symmetric pair, said it satisfied the constraints, then abandoned it on a hand-waved objection and reported something else. So the incumbent's ban on false assumptions is not the binding failure any more -- self-sabotage after a correct check is. I replaced the branch-intersection language with (a) solve constraints simultaneously rather than walking cases, (b) apply each constraint to both members so the symmetric candidate surfaces early, and (c) once a candidate survives every condition, keep it and audit the objection instead.

records.mutation: replace the target/form-specification clause with a route-switching trigger: name the concrete symptoms of ballooning algebra and the cheaper equivalent conditions (moduli, symmetry, degree comparison) to switch to
records.subagent_summary: Seven of eight fresh rollouts were correct at 4.6k-10k tokens each; the single failure was the only one to hit the 16384 cap. It took the parametrize-by-angle route, carried x and y as ratios in cos(theta), and produced a degree-4 mess it could not reduce, then burned the rest of the budget re-verifying sample points and repeatedly declaring the setup impossible. Every winner instead noticed the pinned modulus and reduced the whole problem to one small equation in x and y. Prior rounds already tried tuning the recheck loop and pre-specifying the requested form without gains, so I targeted the earlier decision point: name the symptoms of ballooning algebra as a trigger to switch to a cheaper equivalent condition rather than grinding the expensive route.

records.mutation: replace the abstract bound-plus-witness stop licence with a finite-regime enumeration criterion that makes further parameter sampling provably uninformative, and move the combining arithmetic ahead of any setup recap in the write-up
records.subagent_summary: Only 2 of 8 scored, both by a short write-up that reached the combining step. No failure was mathematical: 7 of 8 held the right overlap inside the first 3-7k of ~52-62k characters, then spent 98-182 rotation re-tests and 45-79 restarts. Four never closed reasoning at all. The two decisive cases did close it but opened with a full setup recap plus multi-heading preamble and were truncated one line short of combining the numbers; one even wrote the correct minimal overlap and then hedged that rotation might reduce it further. So the incumbent's certify clause is too abstract to fire against continuous rotation. This revision gives a concrete, checkable halting test (a continuous parameter has finitely many regimes; once each is named and sampled, more values cannot inform) and orders the write-up so the arithmetic precedes any recap.

records.mutation: state that reuse is permitted unless forbidden, and add a trust-the-derived-product directive against retreating from a bound that looks larger than the given numbers
records.subagent_summary: Fresh 8 rollouts with the incumbent scored 3/8. Two failures argued each polynomial could serve only one called number and answered with the polynomial count; two more computed the per-piece root cap one too low and reported that smaller product; one truncated after explicitly writing the correct product but calling it "too large" and hunting for a smaller intended value. So the residual-degree audit already in the hint is not the binding leak - the leaks are an invented single-use restriction and a refusal to keep a bound that looks bigger than the numbers in the statement. The revision states that reuse is permitted unless the problem forbids it, keeps the per-piece root cap, and adds an explicit instruction to trust the derived product rather than retreat to a rounder or smaller value.

records.mutation: make root screening concrete (substitute into the stated domain condition, not a remembered interval) and add a reversal rule when only a degenerate root survives
records.subagent_summary: Seven of eight fresh rollouts were correct at about 9k tokens; the one failure got the right reduced quadratic and both roots, then mis-screened them from a remembered domain interval, threw away the admissible negative-fraction root, kept the root that makes two named points coincide, and reported a collapsed figure as the value. Every correct rollout instead recognized that root as degenerate and took the other. So the incumbent clause "discard roots that are degenerate or outside the domain" is exactly what backfires: applied from memory it can eliminate the wanted root. I made screening concrete (substitute the number into the stated condition) and added a reversal rule: a degenerate or trivial outcome means the screening was wrong, so restore the other root rather than reporting the collapse.

records.mutation: require the asked-slot paraphrase to be validated against one simulated concrete run before any counting, instead of merely stating the arrival-order fact
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent gave 0/8, down from 0.25 two rounds ago; six of eight rollouts finished normally, so length is not the block. Part (a) is now largely solved: five rollouts derived the correct branch-count denominator from free 50/50 steps. Every single failure was the second part, and always the same one: the student verbally restates the asked slot as "the item handled last", then prices that as 1/n by asserted symmetry. Prior hints stated the arrival-order orientation fact declaratively and the student read past it. This revision instead makes the restatement itself a checkable step: simulate one concrete run, write the destination out in arrival order, and confirm which item occupies the asked slot before any counting begins, and forbids pricing a named-item-in-named-slot event as 1/n.

records.mutation: add free-parameter diagnostic: an unpinnable constant means an unused given, and block the insufficient-data / set-to-zero exits
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling under the incumbent scored 2 of 8. Both successes solved the three smallest instances exactly, read off the signed reciprocal-factorial pattern, and landed. All six failures instead posited a general product-times-linear-factor form with two unspecified constants and tried to pin both from the single non-vanishing condition: five ran to the token cap looping on that, several explicitly concluded there was an infinite family or insufficient data, one forced a constant to zero and gave a wrong value, and the one that terminated dropped a legitimate constraint and landed just off. The revision keeps commit-then-verify and small-instance grounding, but adds the missing diagnostic: a leftover free parameter means an unused given (an absent term, a degree bound, or a value at a special point), and blocks both the insufficient-data and set-it-to-zero exits.

records.mutation: keep the train-safe opening and small-cases clause verbatim; replace the never-exercised exact-fractions clause with an arithmetic-reliability rule (recompute each product/quotient/factorisation by a second decomposition, magnitude plausibility check)
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh rollouts scored reward 1 with clean stops at 3.0-6.0k tokens, so train is saturated and every gain must come from transfer; twelve rounds of scope-labeling, gcd-naming, representation-switching, output-form and uniqueness-forcing edits all failed, and the incumbent's exact-fractions clause is never exercised (no rollout keeps anything as a fraction). What the rollouts actually do is heavy integer work: 11-29 divisor/gcd mentions each, factorisations redone repeatedly, and 5-23 self-interruptions that are almost all arithmetic re-verification rather than strategy doubt. So I swapped the dead clause for the reliability habit the student is already improvising: recompute each multi-digit product, quotient or factorisation by a second decomposition and sanity-check magnitude. Token count 158, measured with the pinned tokenizer.

records.mutation: state the add-step outcome constructively (c is half the sum of the two given numbers) so the numbers cannot be zeroed, name a degenerate center as a sign slip, and reinvest the compressed opening in generic output discipline (exact values, requested form and order)
records.subagent_summary: Seven of eight fresh rollouts were correct, finishing in 4.5k-13k tokens by committing to the shared-center antisymmetric pair and solving the two supplied values by sum and difference. The lone failure reached that exact form immediately, then added the two values as if their right-hand sides were zero, obtained a center of zero, and read that as refutation; it next manufactured a parity objection by dropping the outer sign, and spent the rest of the budget naming coefficients and expanding the degree-nine composition. The revision therefore replaces the passive 'adding must cancel' phrasing with the constructive outcome that the center is half the sum of the two given numbers, so those numbers cannot be discarded, labels a degenerate center a sign slip, and spends tokens freed by compression on guidance that fires on any problem: keep values exact and report precisely what was asked.

records.mutation: ban whole-map construction and replace it with following one single label until it returns, keeping the untraced-disjoint-swaps warning and adding an item-count scaling expectation
records.subagent_summary: 3 of 8 correct. Two clean failure modes. One rollout asserted "a product of disjoint transpositions, so the order is 2" and answered without ever iterating; three more abandoned row tracing to build an explicit position map, produced non-bijective garbage (one index sent to two places), then burned the 16384-token cap re-deriving it, one degenerating into thousands of tokens of literal repetition of the same product. A fifth mis-counted the small sizes and fitted a wrong exponent to them. The incumbent already forbids period-2 talk and demands bijections, but it still invites the whole-map construction that drives the loops, so this revision bans map-building outright and substitutes following one single label until it returns home: cheap, self-checking, and it yields the count directly.
